originality.rationale: Published-results and primary-literature searches revealed independent-jury monotonicity, equicorrelated-vote jury theorems, general dependent-jury asymptotic/equilibrium results, and exact Markov-binomial approximation work. Their inspected assumptions/conclusions do not state or directly imply the all-size stationary-Markov strict-sign law and its pathwise pivotal probability. The 2007 dependent-jury article was inaccessible in full and remains explicitly a substantial priority risk; similarity search failure alone was not treated as novelty evidence.
residual_risks: The full 2007 Berend–Sapir dependent-voter monotonicity paper could have a criterion or worked case that subsumes the Markov specialization; only its abstract was accessible.
Full published Peleg–Zamir and other older general-dependent-jury manuscripts may contain an equivalent theorem under different parameterization.
The result is not independently certified for historical priority.

value.rationale: The result settles natural all-size finite Condorcet monotonicity for an ordered, dependent, nonexchangeable juror population, explicitly including strong anticorrelation. A sharp, simple Markov-switching parameter condition and exact marginal pivotal-event factor enable an analytical check independent of approximate binomial calculations.
